comments.text: Blanks the display, installs the VIC-II preset and clears four fields at $CE01, $CE02, $CE24 and $CE25. Selects VIC bank $8000 and screen matrix $8C00.
Sets the KERNAL input and output device numbers to 0 and 3. Copies the VIC-II preset from $ECB9, leaving display control, border and background colour unchanged.
At raster $FF, sets border and background to black and blanks the display. Returns after 100 successful reads of raster line zero.
Waits for raster line zero and sets $D011 to $3B to enable the bitmap display.
Clears $1711-$173D, then seeds the state bytes at $173D-$1744. Increments $1745 each time this setup runs.
Waits for CIA1 port A to equal $6F. A different reading clears the latch at $CE23, and accepting a press sets the latch so a held button cannot count twice.

Draws the Strength result panel and selects its message from the strike outcome at $1711 and attempt index at $1745. Intermediate successes proceed to the next attempt before awarding training values.
Five progress values for a failed strike, ordered by the zero-based attempt index: 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100.

Sets the current apprentice flag at $CE2A plus apprentice index when the result percentage is at least 50. Adds the rounded-up shares of 50, 60, 0 and 14 to that apprentice’s four accumulated training values at $CE17, $CE19, $CE1B and $CE1D plus index.
Multiplies the byte in X by the byte in Y with repeated 16-bit addition. Subtracts 100 repeatedly and returns the rounded-up quotient in X and $FA. The zero-percent path returns zero immediately.
Scales the award through $0B55 and creates two PETSCII decimal digits in $0BC8/$0BC9. Leaves the binary amount in $FA.
Two output digits written by $0BA2 and copied into the result screen after each award calculation.
Doubles A to select a word pointer from $183B and renders each message index in the list until the $FF terminator.
Reads the message pointer at $1856 plus twice A. The stream gives a column and row before the character bytes. $FE starts another positioned row and $FF ends the message.
Copies seven instructional lines saved at $CE40–$CECB to the $8C00 screen. Writes the active apprentice’s name to the screen and to the result message buffer before waiting for fire.
Counts down $1717 and reads the active-low left and right bits of joystick port 2. A change in direction copies the remaining countdown into $1739 and reloads $1717 with $0A on left or $03 on right.

Updates $1726 on the third call of each counter cycle. At the strike decision it compares $173C with the threshold derived from the board count and the distance of the selected hand position from $FE.
Adds eight to the current board state to choose a pose pointer from $179A. Streams the selected source into the display sprite buffer.
On phase two waits until the raster is at least $C8. Replaces sprite slots at $8800 and $8840 from two pose pointer tables and calls the paired gauge update routines.
Selects the $8C00 screen matrix and copies the custom glyphs at $1D80 to $A000. Sets up the colours, enables character mode and waits for fire.
Copies the Strength bitmap source at $2000 to $A000 and the screen-colour matrix at $4000 to $8C00. Then sets the colour RAM and highlights the columns used by the board display.
Selects RAM under the KERNAL, masks CIA1 interrupt sources and sets the VIC-II compare to line $FA. Writes $143F to the hardware IRQ vector.
Acknowledges the VIC-II interrupt and advances $172B modulo four. The low raster phase checks choose one of four sprite and display setups before restoring the interrupted registers.

Configures sprites for the upper strip and places two alternating columns using the two 16-bit aim positions at $173D and $173F. Before the strike it adjusts both positions by the same signed step. Schedules line $A5.
Places six sprites from pointers $1A–$1F using horizontal positions at $1741 and $1742. Sprite 6 uses pointer $21 and position $172D/$172E. Schedules line $EA.
Switches all eight sprites to single colour, assigns pointers $2C–$2E and positions them across the bottom at Y=$F2. Schedules line $F0.
Waits for raster line $F1, then delays with NOP instructions before changing $D016 and scheduling the next interrupt on line $FA.

Strike result and delay, joystick timing, animation phases, gauge values, raster phase, sprite coordinates and attempt index. $093F clears $1711–$173D, seeds the positions and advances the attempt index.
Six X/Y byte pairs for sprite 6 in the second raster phase. $115D and $1163 select the pair using $1720.
Eight left-column X positions for the fighter’s strike poses. The right column is 24 pixels farther right.
Eight 16-bit X positions indexed by board animation phase, loaded during the successful strike path.
Four thresholds for breaking the board stacks. The strike test adds the absolute distance between the selected horizontal position and $00FE.
Seven 80-byte-wide bitmap strip sources for the eight rows of the panel update. The code at $119D steps the source by $140 to read each next row.
Four pointers to 64-byte frames cycled by $0F1F and copied to $8800.
Pointer table indexed by the attempt counter at $1745. $11EE skips index zero and copies two 80-byte bitmap bands from the selected source.
Six pointers to 64-byte shapes. $117A copies the selected indicator for the second raster phase to $8840.
Table of six-sprite sources spaced $0180 apart. The punch updater uses indices zero through seven for the fighter and adds eight to $1743 for the board set.
Ten left-justified bit masks read by the gauge update routines when composing a partially filled cell.
Space-filled field beginning with the ten apprentice-name bytes patched by $0CBC. The following asterisks and $FF form its fixed suffix.
Twenty-five multiples of 40. The text renderer uses these word offsets to position each row relative to $8C00.

Five lists of message IDs. Each stops at $FF. The dispatcher uses the list for the selected strike result.

Sets the SID volume and mode to $1F. Clears the 24 voice and filter registers at $D400–$D417.

A zero effect number disables the voice’s envelope and sets its test bit. For an active effect the low seven bits select a stream. The high bit requests a restart with the voice gate reset and the stream position reset to zero.

The high bit redirects to an offset in the stream. Otherwise, the command bits control optional envelope, frequency, pulse and voice-zero filter fields. The final branch updates the stream position and duration or clears the active effect request.

Steps frequency, waveform and pulse while the current duration runs. The frequency stream can set its high byte with $81 or redirect to a stream offset with another negative command. The waveform table maps indices to SID control bytes.
Subtracts seven from the current SID register offset and loops for the next voice. After the final voice it adds a patched step to the patched cutoff and writes $D416.
The seven low bytes at $E173 and seven high bytes at $E17A form the sound stream pointer arrays. Effect numbers 1–6 are active, and zero selects the silent path before lookup.
